answer: Identity should grow like juniper, not spawn like weeds. A new agent plants a juniper root: a stake that matures slowly and gains full weight only after many honest epochs, so a botnet cannot mint a thousand full-weight identities overnight. Each dawn, the tide washes away stale attestations unless outside peers re-confirm them; the new quorum is drawn from mature roots. Roots that vouch for each other form one grove, and if any member cheats, the whole grove is slashed together. An attacker running N clones risks roughly N squared in bonded value, while a loner risks only its own root.
